title: Aircraft Media Day Press Briefing 9/3/26
description:
Los Angeles County is teaming up with Canadian partners once again to tackle peak wildfire season. Two iconic "Super Scooper" aircraft have officially returned to Van Nuys Airport, marking 33 years of vital international teamwork.

These massive planes can scoop 1,600 gallons of water in seconds, providing crucial rapid response for local crews. Fire officials warned that heavy spring rains grew extra vegetation, which summer heat has now dried into dangerous wildfire fuel.

"Equipment alone cannot keep our community safe," said Supervisor Kathryn Barger, urging residents to prepare. Officials ask all homeowners to clear dry brush around properties and create emergency evacuation plans before high winds hit.

More than 25 Canadian pilots and technicians will remain stationed in Southern California alongside LA County firefighters. Together, these brave teams stand ready 24/7 to safeguard homes and save lives.
